title: South Africa Beat Australia by an Innings and 31 Runs to Level Series
excerpt: Temba Bavuma's 179 and Marco Jansen's all-round display turned a rain-hit Test at Gqeberha as South Africa bowled Australia out for 99 and 295 to square the three-match series 1-1.
body:
• South Africa beat Australia by an innings and 31 runs in the second Test at St George's Park, Gqeberha, levelling the three-match series 1-1.
  • Captain Temba Bavuma made a career-best 179 as South Africa recovered from 110 for 6 to declare on 425 for 9.
  • Australia were bowled out for 99 in their first innings, with Marco Jansen taking 5 for 33, and made 295 following on despite Travis Head's 121.
  • The deciding third Test starts in five days, with the series level.

South Africa bowled Australia out for 295 in the last session on Thursday to win the second Test at St George's Park in Gqeberha by an innings and 31 runs and level the three-match series at 1-1, completing a victory that had looked improbable two days earlier.

A Recovery Built by Bavuma

Most of the first two days were lost to rain, and South Africa were 110 for 6 when play resumed on the third morning after Australia had sent them in. Bavuma then led the recovery with 179 from 334 balls, with 18 fours and a six, sharing match-changing partnerships with Marco Jansen, who made 85 off 100 balls, and Simon Harmer, who made 82 off 157. South Africa declared on 425 for 9.

Bavuma was named player of the match. His method, he said, was patience.

"We play good old Test cricket, try and wear the opposition down and then take them down when the opportunity presents itself."

— Temba Bavuma, South Africa captain

Australia Collapse, Then Resist

Australia's first innings lasted 42.3 overs. Jansen took 5 for 33, Wiaan Mulder 2 for 14 and Kagiso Rabada 2 for 33 as the tourists were dismissed for 99, with Steve Smith top-scoring with 28 off 88 balls. Jansen became only the second South African since readmission to score a half-century and take five wickets in the same Test against Australia, matching Dale Steyn at the MCG in 2008.

Forced to follow on, Australia resumed on the final day at 156 for 4 after rain wiped out the morning session. Head, 87 not out overnight, reached 121 off 190 balls — his 13th Test century and only his second outside Australia — before chopping a rising Mulder delivery onto his stumps. Smith, batting at number seven after struggling with a neck problem in the first innings, made 3, top-edging a Rabada pull to mid-wicket.

The Final Session

Nightwatchman Scott Boland resisted for 166 balls for a Test-best 40 before Mulder bowled him. Mulder then bowled captain Pat Cummins for 4 in the following over. As dark clouds gathered, Rabada removed Mitchell Starc for 11 and Jansen finished the innings when Josh Hazlewood edged his first ball to the slips.

"We were scrambling a bit, not sure about the weather and Australia made us work hard for those last six wickets," Bavuma said, according to the Reuters report carried by Virgin Radio Dubai.

What It Means

The defeat was Australia's fifth at Gqeberha, a venue where they have not won a Test since 1997. South Africa have now won 28 of the 33 Tests in which they enforced the follow-on. With the series level, the third Test in five days decides the contest — and Bavuma was quick to play down the celebrations: "There's still a job at hand with another match still to go."
